prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for 'adoption, new_flow', 'finish, redesign', and 'sign_in, reorder' changes, as each has only 1 test.
No kind of change can be called helpful yet, as no tests have won.
No clear effect was seen for 'adoption, new_flow' and 'finish, redesign' changes.
Predictions have been consistently too high compared to noise-corrected measurements.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_flow: +0.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, redesign: -1.6% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: -5.6% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [choose_path, redesign] choose_path_split_redesign: Redesign the choose_path screen into a split layout clearly separating ready-to-adopt preset pets from custom pet generation. (why: choose_path has a 23.8% dropoff rate and a high mean completion time of 514s, indicating confusion during path selection.)
1: [home, new_flow] interactive_waiting_flow: Add an interactive waiting room sub-flow with mini-games while the desktop pet is generating in the background. (why: The waiting screen has a high median duration of 201s and mean of 2336s, causing dropoff while users wait idle.)
2: [finish, new_screen] pet_shortcut_guide_screen: Insert a dedicated hotkey and system tray control guide screen right before finishing onboarding. (why: Support received 3 confusion emails regarding how to hide, show, or control the pet once setup concludes.)
3: [sign_in, hint] sign_in_progress_sync_hint: Add a prominent explanatory hint explaining that signing in protects pets from being lost or reset. (why: 8 support requests reported lost or reset pets upon signing back in later.)
4: [home, wait_info] waiting_time_estimate_info: Display an estimated progress timer and active status updates on the waiting screen. (why: Users stay on the home waiting screen for up to 2336s on average; explicit time estimates reduce perceived friction.)
5: [home, notification] waiting_desktop_ready_notification: Add an option to send a OS desktop notification when pet generation completes in the background. (why: Mean waiting time is 2336s; desktop notifications let users switch to other tasks without abandoning the app.)
6: [finish, layout] home_intro_spotlight_layout: Switch the home_intro screen to a spotlight layout focused on activating the pet on the desktop. (why: 35.2% of users drop off at finish, and 3 support emails reported pets failing to appear on desktop.)
7: [adoption, copy] upload_photos_guidance_copy: Update photo upload body text with clearer formatting requirements to prevent rendering glitches. (why: Support logged 3 issues where custom pet generation failed or produced visually glitched results.)

scores.note: Choose_path loses 23.8% with 514s mean time, but major layout redesigns show weak or negative results so far.
Home dropoff is 18.7% with long wait times, but building a mini-game flow is expensive and unproven.
Finish loses 35.2% and 3 support emails exist, but adding another screen right before completion increases friction.
Sign_in loses 27.1% and has 8 support requests; adding explanatory copy is low cost and addresses a clear concern.
Home step has a 2336s mean time; adding progress estimates sets expectations with moderate implementation effort.
Desktop notifications help users switch tasks during 2336s average wait times without abandoning the app.
Finish loses 35.2% and has 3 support mails, but layout redesigns on finish previously regressed conversion.
Adoption has the highest step dropoff (39.1%) and support reports photo glitches; low-cost copy guidance directly targets dropoff.
